svg.title: From Filing to Certified Letters
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-filing-to-letters-roadmap; chapter number: 1; chart type: process_flow; title: From Filing to Certified Letters; subtitle: The court sequence that must finish before any estate property is listed; caption: Nothing moves on an estate property until the court issues letters; the letters date is the date the property can be listed.; assumptions note: Timing figures are attributed practitioner claims. SwiftProbate cites 2 to 6 weeks for letters in straightforward cases and several months for busy courts or contested cases; California timelines run longer.; note: Sequence per SwiftProbate, RLS Law Corporation, California Probate Real Estate Made Simple, and NOVA Real Estate Solutions.; stages: step: 01; label: File in the county of domicile; value: Step 1; detail: Original will, certified death certificate, petition and fee; request full IAEA authority at filing to avoid repeat court approvals.; step: 02; label: Notify every heir and publish; value: Step 2; detail: List every heir and relative, including disinherited ones; the DE121 notice is mailed by a non-party with proof filed.; step: 03; label: Clear the hearing; value: Step 3; detail: An omitted heir is the most common avoidable mistake, and the judge will continue the hearing.; step: 04; label: Pull certified letters; value: Step 4; detail: Order at least 5 to 10 certified copies; some institutions refuse letters more than sixty to ninety days old.; step: 05; label: Open the estate account under its EIN; value: Step 5; detail: Estate money runs only through this account, and debts are paid in statutory priority order to avoid personal liability.
